content.value_statement: Payment systems must protect funds while coordinating channels, ledgers, callbacks, refunds, and reconciliation. This skill provides architecture patterns, security controls, diagnostics, and delivery templates.
actual_capabilities: Design layered payment architectures covering access, transactions, accounting, settlement, and channel services.
Define provider-neutral channel adapters for payments, queries, refunds, and callbacks.
Model transaction states, idempotency controls, and distributed consistency strategies.
Plan reconciliation workflows that match internal transactions with channel bills and identify differences.
Recommend payment security, data protection, risk controls, and high-availability practices.
Diagnose missing callbacks, duplicate payments, and reconciliation mismatches with structured checklists.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not an executable payment integration.
Does not verify current provider APIs, fees, regional rules, or certification requirements.
Does not replace PCI DSS, legal, accounting, or independent security review.
The sample reconciliation logic omits production concerns such as currencies, rounding, duplicates, and persistence.

use_cases.title: Design a Payment Service
use_cases.description: Create transaction states, idempotency controls, channel boundaries, and failure handling for a new payment service.

use_cases.title: Review Payment Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess consistency, accounting, availability, security, and reconciliation decisions before implementation.

use_cases.title: Investigate Transaction Differences
use_cases.description: Build a focused checklist for missing callbacks, duplicate payments, or unmatched channel records.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Payment Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main layers of a payment system and the responsibility of each layer.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Channel Adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a provider-neutral adapter for payment, query, refund, and callback operations. Include failure handling and idempotency.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Payment Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a diagnostic plan for [incident]. Consider callbacks, signatures, state transitions, retries, idempotency, and reconciliation evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Advanced Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this payment architecture: [details]. Identify fund-safety, consistency, scaling, security, observability, and recovery risks with prioritized recommendations.

output_examples.input: Design an idempotent payment flow for merchant orders.
output_examples.output: Use a unique merchant and order key, persist the first result, reject conflicting payloads, and return the stored result for retries.

output_examples.input: Investigate a customer charge that remains pending.
output: Confirm the provider status and callback delivery.
Verify callback signatures, retry queues, and allowed state transitions.
Compare internal records with the provider bill before correcting state.

output_examples.output: Report totals, matched records, internal-only records, channel-only records, amount differences, causes, owners, and resolution status.

best_practices: Supply transaction states, provider behavior, consistency requirements, and failure scenarios in each request.
Validate every recommendation against provider documentation, compliance duties, and internal accounting controls.
Test retries, duplicate callbacks, timeouts, partial failures, and reconciliation recovery before release.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample code as production-ready payment or accounting logic.
Do not store card data, credentials, or private keys in prompts.
Do not update financial state without idempotency, audit records, and reconciliation evidence.

faq.question: Which payment topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers architecture, channels, transactions, distributed consistency, reconciliation, risk controls, security, performance, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it integrate directly with payment providers?
faq.answer: No. It provides provider-neutral designs and review guidance, but it does not call provider APIs.

faq.question: Which programming languages are represented?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Java, Go, and Python systems, with small Java and Python examples.

faq.question: Can it replace a PCI DSS assessment?
faq.answer: No. Use qualified compliance and security professionals for certification, scope decisions, and production review.

faq.question: Can it help with payment incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It offers checklists for missing callbacks, duplicate payments, failed transactions, and reconciliation differences.

faq.question: What context improves its recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide transaction states, provider behavior, data flows, failure symptoms, consistency goals, volumes, and compliance constraints.
